title: Six-functor operation stage structures
statement: Fix finite-field data [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell$ different from the characteristic, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a positive integer $n$. Let $\mathscr S$ be the category of finite-type schemes over the specified algebraic closure of the finite field, with morphisms over that field [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The coefficient categories are the bounded finite-torsion constructible categories [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the derived-complete integral categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], their rationalizations [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the common-stage algebraically closed coefficient categories [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], with finite-Tor domains [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. A construction stage on a family of categories $\mathscr B(X)$ consists of pullback and direct image with their adjunction [def-weil-derived-direct-image], extension by zero for open immersions [def-weil-extension-by-zero], compact-support functors for each compactification [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], comparison and composition isomorphisms, identity and cocycle equations as in [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], and proper and open identifications. It includes exceptional right adjoints and compatibility of their units and counits [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], without assuming ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]. A compactified Cartesian square consists of its four finite-type schemes, its Cartesian square, and compatible Cartesian squares for the open and proper factors. Exchange-stage data realizes the exchange and projection composites [def-exchange-projection] on the supplied operations and tensor, with the pullback-composition comparisons and proper/open identifications. Coefficient-change data consists of operation comparisons preserving adjunction units, counits and compactification comparisons, and comparison squares for the three transformations. The tensor and bounded-output internal Hom are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Duality data consists of the coefficient unit and the assertion that internal Hom into its exceptional image lies in the specified bounded-output domain; the dualizing object and Verdier dual are then defined by those operations. At integral coefficients, compact support is realized by the coherent strict reduction tower and normalized total derived inverse limit [def-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-datum]; the rational and common-stage compact-support values are those of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. These records specify construction data and assert no existence theorem. Integral construction maps are normalized after every positive quotient reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]: support and direct-image comparisons are the scalar-adjunction transposes of the specified Roos projections [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action], pullback comparison is the projection-normalized K-flat representative comparison, and open-extension comparison is the canonical scalar-adjunction mate [def-sf-open-reduction-coefficient-mate]. These same comparisons preserve compactification changes, composition, proper and open identifications, pullback composition, and both ordinary adjunction units and counits. Rationalization and common-stage inclusion preserve all these maps; their pullback, direct-image, support and open-extension comparisons are the identities on the specified integral and finite-stage object models.
